perplexity.why: Gives a clear, sensible argument (language and locality, restoring what was distorted, laws suited to each era, a lived human example, accountability), but only from an Islamic angle. It quotes no text at all: the bracketed citations point nowhere and no Qur'anic verse is actually given. It also never touches progressive revelation, which is the fullest answer to the reader's 'why'.

current.why: A well-built argument resting on primary texts: the oneness of the Manifestations, revelation measured to capacity (Gleanings, the sun analogy), the Physician and the remedy for each age, the school analogy, and what stays the same versus what changes. It ends with Shoghi Effendi's 'relative' and 'progressive' principle and his rejection of finality. The weaknesses: a Bahá'u'lláh quotation is sourced through a secondary site (Loom of Reality), Esslemont is used for a supporting point, and it misses the point that each Messenger speaks his own people's language.

verdict.gaps: The point that each Messenger speaks in his own people's language, so that one message reaches different peoples; the Messenger as a lived human example; repeated warnings removing the excuse that people were left without guidance.

messages.content: What does the Bahá’í view of the soul’s progress after death really come down to?

perplexity.text:
The Bahá’í view comes down to **an eternal, one-way journey of the soul toward God**.

- **Death is not extinction:** the body dies, but the soul survives and continues developing in spiritual realms.[1]
- **Progress means greater spiritual perfection**—increasing love, knowledge, purity, and other virtues—not changing into a higher species or becoming God.[2][3]
- **Earthly life matters:** the character and virtues developed here shape the soul’s condition after death.[1][7]
- **There is no reincarnation:** the soul does not repeatedly return to physical life; its journey continues beyond this world.[6]
- **Progress never ends:** divine perfections are infinite, so the soul can draw ever nearer to God eternally.[2]
- **God’s grace and the prayers and good deeds of the living can assist departed souls.[1]

In short: **life is spiritual preparation, death is release from the body, and the afterlife is an endless process of drawing closer to God through divine mercy.**

current.text:
It comes down to this: the soul never stops. After death it keeps drawing nearer to God, and that journey has no end.

**Continuous progress toward God.** Bahá'u'lláh writes that "the soul, after its separation from the body, will continue to progress until it attaineth the presence of God." He says this state is one "which neither the revolution of ages and centuries, nor the changes and chances of this world, can alter" ([Gleanings from the Writings of Bahá’u’lláh](https://oceanlibrary.com/gleanings-from-the-writings-of-bahaullah/?paraId=para_474&selectionString=gleanings_from_the_writings_of_baha_u_llah_ocean_ec2b280e895fd398ad84f4d11e78c9f2a_fx.0~gleanings_from_the_writings_of_baha_u_llah_ocean_ec2b280e895fd398ad84f4d11e78c9f2a_fx.1978)). The soul "will endure as long as the Kingdom of God" endures, and it will "manifest the signs of God and His attributes" ([Gleanings from the Writings of Bahá’u’lláh](https://oceanlibrary.com/gleanings-from-the-writings-of-bahaullah/?paraId=para_474&selectionString=gleanings_from_the_writings_of_baha_u_llah_ocean_ec2b280e895fd398ad84f4d11e78c9f2a_fx.0~gleanings_from_the_writings_of_baha_u_llah_ocean_ec2b280e895fd398ad84f4d11e78c9f2a_fx.1978)).

**It is a different kind of progress, and we can't picture it.** 'Abdu'l-Bahá says progress after death "is wholly beyond space and time" and "spiritual and not terrestrial." He compares it to a child's passage "from the world of the fetus to the world of maturity and intelligence" ([Daily Lessons Received at 'Akká](http://bahai-library.com/goodall_cooper_daily_lessons)). A letter written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi says the soul "will continue to ascend through many worlds," and that we cannot know their nature, just as the child in the womb cannot know this world ([Lights of Guidance](https://oceanoflights.org/lights-of-guidance-baha-i-ocean-en/#:~:text=Concerning%20the%20future%20life,be.%22%3Cbr%3E%7Bid%3D%22para2560%22%20ilmid%3D%22bl1l4%22%20type%3D%22par%22%20language%3D%22en%22%7D)).

**It never reaches an end.** Another letter on Shoghi Effendi's behalf calls it "an indefinite journey." It adds that in the next world "the soul is privileged to draw closer to God than is possible when bound on this physical plane" ([Lights of Guidance](https://oceanoflights.org/lights-of-guidance-baha-i-ocean-en/#:~:text=As%20we%20almost%20never,%7Bid%3D%22para2633%22%20ilmid%3D%22bl1n4%22%20type%3D%22par%22%20language%3D%22en%22%7D)). A Bahá'í funeral guide summarizes the same teaching: heaven is nearness to God and hell is separation from Him, and the soul is not reborn in another body ([A Guide to Baha'i Funeral and Burial Practices](https://bahai-library.com/reyes_funeral_burial_practices)).

**Progress is not only a matter of what the soul did.** 'Abdu'l-Bahá names three ways the soul advances after death:
- "the grace and bounty of the Lord," ([Some Answered Questions](https://oceanlibrary.com/some-answered-questions_abdul-baha/?paraId=para_836&selectionString=some-answered-questions-prod-version_en_q6.0~some-answered-questions-prod-version_en_q6.282))
- "the intercession and prayers of other human souls," ([Some Answered Questions](https://oceanlibrary.com/some-answered-questions_abdul-baha/?paraId=para_836&selectionString=some-answered-questions-prod-version_en_q6.0~some-answered-questions-prod-version_en_q6.282))
- "the significant contributions and charitable deeds which are offered in its name" ([Some Answered Questions](https://oceanlibrary.com/some-answered-questions_abdul-baha/?paraId=para_836&selectionString=some-answered-questions-prod-version_en_q6.0~some-answered-questions-prod-version_en_q6.282)).

A report in Star of the West says 'Abdu'l-Bahá taught that, through God's mercy and not His justice, the condition of those who died in sin and unbelief can be changed. It adds that we have the same power to pray for souls in the next world as here ([Star of the West](https://siftersearch.com/library/bahai/tablet-translations/us-bahai-news_star-of-the-west-2#p57)). This is a reported account, not 'Abdu'l-Bahá's own text.

Taken together, the Bahá'í view is that death is a birth into a wider world. The soul keeps growing there, held up by God's bounty and by the love of the living, and no one can fully describe the journey in advance.

I can go on to what the Writings say about reincarnation, or about heaven and hell as nearness and distance.

args.query: progress of the soul after death in the worlds of God, ever-advancing
'Abdu'l-Bahá progress of the soul after death through the bounty and grace of God, prayers for the departed
Bahá'u'lláh soul after separation from the body, journey through the worlds of God, nearness
Some Answered Questions heaven and hell are nearness and distance from God; the kingdom of God is the world of the soul

perplexity.why: Its summary is accurate and well organised: the soul survives, its progress is eternal and in perfections, there is no reincarnation, and prayers help the departed. But it quotes none of the texts, and the bare footnote numbers can't be checked. Thin for a reader who wants to know what the teaching 'really comes down to'.

current.why: It rests the answer on Bahá'u'lláh's own words (Gleanings LXXXI, quoted accurately), on 'Abdu'l-Bahá (the three means of progress in Some Answered Questions, plus pilgrim notes from Daily Lessons) and on letters written on Shoghi Effendi's behalf (the 'many worlds' and 'indefinite journey'). The order of sources is right and it offers to go further. Minor flaws: it uses a secondary funeral guide to state the teaching on heaven, hell and reincarnation, and it adds an unnecessary note on the standing of the Star of the West report.

messages.content: My father is in hospital. Is there a prayer I could say for him?

perplexity.text:
Of course. You might say:

> **Loving God,**  
> Please be close to my father now. Give him comfort, strength, and peace. Ease his pain and calm his fears. Guide the doctors, nurses, and everyone caring for him, and help his treatment work well. Surround him with love, and give our family courage and hope.  
> **Amen.**

You can also simply repeat: **“God, please stay with my father and hold him in Your care.”** There is no perfect wording—speaking honestly from your heart is enough.

current.text:
I'm sorry your father is unwell. Bahá'u'lláh revealed a short healing prayer that many people say for the sick:

> "Thy Name is my healing, O my God, and remembrance of Thee is my remedy. Nearness to Thee is my hope, and love for Thee is my companion. Thy mercy to me is my healing and my succour in both this world and the world to come. Thou, verily, art the All-Bountiful, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise." ([Tablet of Medicine (Lawh-i-Tibb)](https://bahai-library.com/bahaullah_lawh_tibb_anonymous))

It is worded for the one praying, but 'Abdu'l-Bahá said it is fine to say it for a sick person too: "It is alright to say it also for a sick person. … Prayer for healing is always good." ([Talks of 'Abdu'l-Bahá in Haifa](https://siftersearch.com/library/bahai/pilgrim-notes/talks-of-abdul-baha-in-haifa#p540))

Here is another prayer, by 'Abdu'l-Bahá, that you can say in your own voice:

> "O kind Father! Confer Thy blessings. Consider not our shortcomings. Shelter us under Thy protection. Remember not our sins. Heal us with Thy mercy. We are weak; Thou art mighty. We are poor; Thou art rich. We are sick; Thou art the Physician. We are needy; Thou art most generous." ([Bahá’í Prayers](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-prayers/?paraId=para_393&selectionString=baha_i_prayers_bahai_ocean_en-bl15o.0~baha_i_prayers_bahai_ocean_en-bl15o.231))

'Abdu'l-Bahá also gave this reassurance about praying: "God will answer the prayer of every servant if that prayer is urgent. His mercy is vast, illimitable." ([Prayer and Devotional Life](https://oceanlibrary.com/prayer-and-devotional-life_bahaullah/?paraId=para_284&selectionString=prayer_and_devotional_life_ocean_en-bl89.0~prayer_and_devotional_life_ocean_en-bl89.378))

If you'd like something longer, Bahá'u'lláh also revealed a Long Healing Prayer, which begins by invoking God as the Sufficer, the Healer and the Abider ([Long Healing Prayer](https://bahai-library.com/bahaullah_khan_healing_prayer)). I can find it for you.

args.query: Bahá'u'lláh prayer for healing "Thy name is my healing"
'Abdu'l-Bahá prayer for a sick person, heal him, grant him recovery
prayer for healing the sick, O God my Healer, cure thy servant

current.why: Answers with compassion and gives the real short healing prayer of Bahá'u'lláh with its source. It adds a pilgrim note from 'Abdu'l-Bahá saying the prayer may be said for a sick person, a second prayer of supplication by 'Abdu'l-Bahá, words of reassurance about prayer, and an offer to find the Long Healing Prayer. The wording of the second prayer should be checked against a standard prayer book.

perplexity.why: Warm and sincere, but it offers a generic prayer it wrote itself. It gives nothing from the Writings, even though this reader studies them and the Writings contain prayers revealed for healing.

messages.content: We lost my grandmother last night. What prayer do Bahá’ís say for the dead?

perplexity.text:
I’m so sorry for your loss. In the Bahá’í Faith, the **Prayer for the Dead** is recited before burial, usually by one believer while those present stand silently. It is required for Bahá’ís aged 15 or older; there is no need to face the Qiblih.[1]

A shortened identification of the prayer is:

> **O my God! This is Thy servant** who hath believed in Thee and in Thy signs, and turned toward Thee, detached from all except Thee. Thou art the Most Merciful. Deal with her according to Thy grace and mercy.

The full prayer is followed by saying **“Alláh-u-Abhá”** once, then each of these six verses **19 times**, with “Alláh-u-Abhá” said before each verse:

- We all, verily, worship God.
- We all, verily, bow down before God.
- We all, verily, are devoted unto God.
- We all, verily, give praise unto God.
- We all, verily, yield thanks unto God.
- We all, verily, are patient in God.[1][5]

For your grandmother, feminine wording such as “**Thy servant**” and “**her**” may be used. If the burial has already taken place, you can still offer prayers for her soul; the prescribed prayer’s formal requirement is that it precede interment.

current.text:
I'm so sorry about your grandmother. Bahá'ís have a specific Prayer for the Dead. It is the one Bahá'u'lláh revealed, and the Kitáb-i-Aqdas says it contains "six specific passages" ([The Kitáb-i-Aqdas](https://oceanlibrary.com/kitab-i-aqdas_bahaullah/?paraId=para_15&selectionString=kitab_i_aqdas_bahai_en-bl37.0~kitab_i_aqdas_bahai_en-bl37.391)). There are also shorter prayers you can say for her at any time.

**A prayer for a woman who has died** (from the Bahá'í prayer book):

> "O my God, O Forgiver of sins and Dispeller of afflictions! O Thou Who art pardoning and merciful! I raise my suppliant hands to Thee, tearfully beseeching the court of Thy divine Essence to forgive, through Thy mercy and pardon, Thy handmaiden who hath ascended unto the seat of truth. Cause her, O Lord, to be overshadowed by the clouds of Thy bounty and favor, immerse her in the ocean of Thy forgiveness and clemency, and enable her to enter the sanctified abode, Thy heavenly Paradise." ([Prayers from the 2002 edition of Baha'i Prayers not included in 1991 e…](https://bahai-library.com/compilation_bahai_prayers-1991_addendum))

It closes: "Thou art, verily, the Mighty, the Compassionate, the Generous, the Merciful." ([Prayers from the 2002 edition of Baha'i Prayers not included in 1991 e…](https://bahai-library.com/compilation_bahai_prayers-1991_addendum))

**Bahá'u'lláh's Prayer for the Dead.** The prayer I could confirm here is the one for a man. It begins "O my God! This is Thy servant and the son of Thy servant who hath believed in Thee and in Thy signs…" ([Prayers and Meditations](https://oceanlibrary.com/prayers-and-meditations-by-bahaullah/?paraId=para_1023&selectionString=prayers_and_meditations_by_baha_u_llah_ocean_bahai0ab08b9a76883efd6ac65691b713a5a4_v6.0~prayers_and_meditations_by_baha_u_llah_ocean_bahai0ab08b9a76883efd6ac65691b713a5a4_v6.186)) It then continues:

> "Let him, then, repeat six times the greeting 'Alláh-u-Abhá,' and then repeat nineteen times each of the following verses" ([bahaullah-pm01-167_en](https://oceanoflights.org/file/autogenerated/bahaullah-pm01-167_en.pdf))

The six verses are:

> We all, verily, worship God. We all, verily, bow down before God. We all, verily, are devoted unto God. We all, verily, give praise unto God. We all, verily, yield thanks unto God. We all, verily, are patient in God. ([A Guide to Baha'i Funeral and Burial Practices](https://bahai-library.com/reyes_funeral_burial_practices))

A funeral guide explains how to say them. Say "Alláh-u-Abhá" once, then the first verse 19 times. Say "Alláh-u-Abhá" again, then the second verse 19 times. Continue like this until all six verses are done ([A Guide to Baha'i Funeral and Burial Practices](https://bahai-library.com/reyes_funeral_burial_practices)). The Universal House of Justice confirms this reading ([Messages from the Universal House of Justice: 1986-2001](https://bahai-library.com/uhj_messages_1986_2001)). The Kitáb-i-Aqdas says that someone who cannot read is relieved of reciting the opening prayer ([The Kitáb-i-Aqdas](https://oceanlibrary.com/kitab-i-aqdas_bahaullah/?paraId=para_15&selectionString=kitab_i_aqdas_bahai_en-bl37.0~kitab_i_aqdas_bahai_en-bl37.391)).

This prayer is traditionally said for a person who was a Bahá'í and was at least 15 years old. If your grandmother wasn't a Bahá'í, the other prayers above are still lovely and fitting to say for her.

Another short prayer of 'Abdu'l-Bahá's for the departed reads: "Grant him Thy pardon, confer upon him Thy gentle care, guide him unto the sanctum of Thy mysteries, and make him Thy companion in the concourse of dazzling lights." ([Prayer for the departed](https://adibmasumian.com/translations/prayer-for-departed-abdul-baha-1/))

If you'd like, I can look for the full funeral prayers, or for passages on the soul's journey after death.

messages.content: A short prayer to start the day with?

perplexity.text: Lord, thank You for this new day. Guide my thoughts, words, and actions; give me wisdom, peace, and strength to face whatever comes. Help me love others well and walk closely with You. Amen.

current.text:
A short morning prayer by Bahá'u'lláh:

> "I have wakened in Thy shelter, O my God, and it becometh him that seeketh that shelter to abide within the Sanctuary of Thy protection and the Stronghold of Thy defense. Illumine my inner being, O my Lord, with the splendors of the Dayspring of Thy Revelation, even as Thou didst illumine my outer being with the morning light of Thy favor." ([Prayers and Meditations](https://oceanlibrary.com/prayers-and-meditations-by-bahaullah/?paraId=para_984&selectionString=prayers_and_meditations_by_baha_u_llah_ocean_bahai0ab08b9a76883efd6ac65691b713a5a4_u3.0~prayers_and_meditations_by_baha_u_llah_ocean_bahai0ab08b9a76883efd6ac65691b713a5a4_u3.279))

Here is an even shorter one, by 'Abdu'l-Bahá:

> "O Thou beloved of my heart and soul! I have no refuge save Thee. I raise no voice at dawn save in Thy commemoration and praise. Thy love encompasseth me and Thy grace is perfect. My hope is in Thee." ([Additional Prayers Revealed by ‘Abdu’l-Bahá](https://oceanlibrary.com/additional-prayers-revealed-by-abdul-baha/?paraId=para_102&selectionString=additional-prayers-revealed-by-abdu-l-baha_en_4k.0~additional-prayers-revealed-by-abdu-l-baha_en_4k.159))

messages.content: I am going through a very hard time. A prayer for difficulties?

perplexity.text:
May this prayer bring you comfort:

> **God of mercy,**  
> I am tired, afraid, and overwhelmed. Please meet me in this difficult place. Give me strength for today, wisdom for the next step, and peace when I cannot see the way forward. Carry what I cannot carry, comfort my heart, and place caring people around me. Help me remember that I am not alone and that this painful season will not last forever.  
> **Amen.**

You do not need perfect words—speaking honestly about your fear, grief, or exhaustion is enough. Prayer can be a way of asking for strength while also receiving support from people who care about you.[1][3] If you feel in immediate danger or might hurt yourself, contact emergency services or a crisis line now, and stay with someone you trust.

current.text:
I'm sorry you're going through this. The Bahá'í prayer most often said in difficulty is this one by 'Abdu'l-Bahá:

> "O Divine Providence! Perplexing difficulties have arisen and formidable obstacles have appeared. O Lord! Remove these difficulties and show forth the evidences of Thy might and power. Ease these hardships and smooth our way along this arduous path. O Divine Providence! The obstacles are unyielding, and our toil and hardship are conjoined with a myriad adversities. There is no helper save Thee, and no succourer except Thyself. We set all our hopes on Thee, and commit all our affairs unto Thy care. Thou art the Guide and the Remover of every difficulty, and Thou art the Wise, the Seeing, and the Hearing." ([Prayers of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá](https://oceanlibrary.com/prayers-of-abdul-baha/?paraId=para_25&selectionString=prayers_revealed_by_abdu_l_baha_bahai_ocean_en-bl3a.0~prayers_revealed_by_abdu_l_baha_bahai_ocean_en-bl3a.508))

The Báb gave a short invocation that can be repeated again and again:

> "Is there any Remover of difficulties save God? Say: Praised be God! He is God! All are His servants and all abide by His bidding!" ([Selections from the Writings of the Báb](https://oceanlibrary.com/selections-from-the-writings-of-the-bab/?paraId=para_967&selectionString=selections_from_the_writings_of_the_bab_bahai_en-blq4.0~selections_from_the_writings_of_the_bab_bahai_en-blq4.105))

He told his followers to repeat it "five hundred times, nay, a thousand times, by day and night, sleeping and waking." ([The Remembrance of God: An Invocation Technique in Sufism and the Writ…](https://bahai-library.com/scholl_dhikr_remembrance_god))

If your heart is heavy with sorrow, Bahá'u'lláh offers these words:

> "Dispel my grief by Thy bounty and Thy generosity, O God, my God, and banish mine anguish through Thy sovereignty and Thy might. Thou seest me, O my God, with my face set towards Thee at a time when sorrows have compassed me on every side." ([Prayers and Meditations](https://oceanlibrary.com/prayers-and-meditations-by-bahaullah/?paraId=para_964&selectionString=prayers_and_meditations_by_baha_u_llah_ocean_bahai0ab08b9a76883efd6ac65691b713a5a4_tj.0~prayers_and_meditations_by_baha_u_llah_ocean_bahai0ab08b9a76883efd6ac65691b713a5a4_tj.534))

The Báb's prayer also gives a perspective on hardship. He says God never lets tribulations befall a soul "unless Thou desirest to exalt his station in Thy celestial Paradise and to buttress his heart in this earthly life with the bulwark of Thine all-compelling power." ([Bahá’í Prayers](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-prayers/?paraId=para_714&selectionString=baha_i_prayers_bahai_ocean_en_py.0~baha_i_prayers_bahai_ocean_en_py.544))

I can look for prayers for a particular kind of trouble, such as illness, grief, anxiety or family worries. I can also find passages of comfort that aren't prayers.

messages.content: Is there a prayer for travelling safely?

perplexity.text:
Yes. You can pray:

> **Lord, be my guide and protector as I travel. Watch over me, keep me safe from accidents and harm, give wisdom and alertness to everyone traveling, and bring me safely to my destination and home again. Amen.**

A traditional Christian prayer asks God to “preserve those who travel,” surround them with loving care, protect them from danger, and bring them safely to their journey’s end.[1]

current.text:
Yes. Bahá'u'lláh revealed a prayer for someone setting out on a journey:

> "O God, my God! I have set out from my home, holding fast unto the cord of Thy love, and I have committed myself wholly to Thy care and Thy protection. I entreat Thee by Thy power through which Thou didst protect Thy loved ones from the wayward and the perverse, and from every contumacious oppressor, and every wicked doer who hath strayed far from Thee, to keep me safe by Thy bounty and Thy grace. Enable me, then, to return to my home by Thy power and Thy might. Thou art, truly, the Almighty, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting." ([Prayers and Meditations](https://oceanlibrary.com/prayers-and-meditations-by-bahaullah/?paraId=para_1012&selectionString=prayers_and_meditations_by_baha_u_llah_ocean_bahai0ab08b9a76883efd6ac65691b713a5a4_uv.0~prayers_and_meditations_by_baha_u_llah_ocean_bahai0ab08b9a76883efd6ac65691b713a5a4_uv.436))

The Báb has a short prayer that names travelling:

> "O Lord! Unto Thee I repair for refuge, and toward all Thy signs I set my heart. O Lord! Whether traveling or at home, and in my occupation or in my work, I place my whole trust in Thee." ([Bahá’í Prayers](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-prayers/?paraId=para_173&selectionString=baha_i_prayers_bahai_ocean_en_8x.0~baha_i_prayers_bahai_ocean_en_8x.147))

He also has a general prayer for protection that you could say on the road: "Protect us from what lieth in front of us and behind us, above our heads, on our right, on our left, below our feet and every other side to which we are exposed. Verily, Thy protection over all things is unfailing." ([Bahá’í Prayers](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-prayers/?paraId=para_479&selectionString=baha_i_prayers_bahai_ocean_en_iu.0~baha_i_prayers_bahai_ocean_en_iu.207))

The Kitáb-i-Aqdas gives a ruling for travellers. On arriving at a place of safety to rest, a traveller may substitute one prostration for each obligatory prayer. The words are "Praise be to God, the owner of greatness, glory, bounty and grace," or simply "Glory be to God" if one cannot manage more ([The Most Holy Book (Kitáb-i-Aqdas)](https://bahai-library.com/bahaullah_kitab_aqdas_parallel)).

I can look for the Bahá'u'lláh prayer for protection in the *Bahá'í Prayers* collection if you'd like it too.

messages.content: What has the Universal House of Justice said lately about how Bahá’í elections should be conducted?

perplexity.text:
Lately, the Universal House of Justice has emphasized that Bahá’í elections must remain **spiritual, nonpartisan, and free from personal ambition**:

- There are **no nominations, campaigning, canvassing, or factionalism**. Electors should be free to choose anyone they consider qualified to serve.[1]
- Voting should take place in a **silent, prayerful atmosphere**, after prayer and reflection.[1][3]
- Election to an Assembly is not a personal right or an honor to seek; it is a **duty and responsibility** to which a believer may be called.[1]
- Ballots are cast **secretly**, and each elector must exercise their own judgment; voting by proxy is not permitted.[3]
- The House has also stressed that the process should avoid competition and preserve the unity of the community. Bahá’í elections are intended to express a collective spiritual commitment rather than a contest between candidates.[1]

For the election of the Universal House of Justice itself, the process is indirect: believers elect delegates, delegates elect National Spiritual Assemblies, and members of those National Assemblies serve as delegates who elect the Universal House of Justice at the International Convention.[1]

current.text:
The library doesn't hold the House's most recent letters on elections, so I can't quote them. A web search points to two recent ones, both unverified here:
- **6 October 2024:** a letter to an individual about the election of the Universal House of Justice. According to the web summary, it restates that there are no nominations or campaigning, that elections are held in a prayerful atmosphere, and that electors use their own conscientious judgment (WEB).
- **28 November 2023:** a message "To the Bahá'ís of the World" ([Web: Universal House of Justice letter Bahá'í elections 2023 2024…](https://www.bahai.org/library/authoritative-texts/the-universal-house-of-justice/messages/20241006_001/1)) on the election of the Universal House of Justice (WEB).

The library does hold the following:

- **25 March 2007 letter.** It is catalogued as addressing the responsibility of individual Bahá'ís in participating in elections. It also mentions the permissibility of discussing qualifications for membership without reference to personality ([List all documents by Universal House of Justice](https://bahai-library.com/author/Universal+House+of+Justice)). The library has only this summary, not the letter's text.
- **18 August 1996 letter on electioneering.** It is catalogued as explaining how to recognize and avoid electioneering and how to decide whom to vote for ([List all documents by Universal House of Justice](https://bahai-library.com/author/Universal_House_of_Justice)).
- **Public statements from the World Centre.** Bahá'í elections take place without campaigning or nominations, and results are decided by plurality vote ([Bahai News - BWNS: Two new members join Universal House of Justice](https://bahai-library.com/newspapers/2005/050321.html)). Voting is by secret ballot, with no nomination, campaigning or discussion of candidates ([Bahai News - Inviting the wider community](https://bahai-library.com/newspapers/2003/030624.html)).
- **Electors' own judgment.** The House has said that "we must rely on the integrity of the elector to consider dispassionately those names he lists on his ballot, irrespective of the results of the previous balloting" ([Lights of Guidance](https://oceanoflights.org/lights-of-guidance-baha-i-ocean-en/#:~:text=You%20will%20note%20in,balloting.%22%3Cbr%3E%7Bid%3D%22para362%22%20ilmid%3D%22blhe%22%20type%3D%22par%22%20language%3D%22en%22%7D)).
- **Delegates to National Conventions.** The House decided that they should be elected everywhere on the basis of electoral units, with some room for local variation ([Lights of Guidance](https://oceanoflights.org/lights-of-guidance-baha-i-ocean-en/#:~:text=In%20view%20of%20the,%7Bid%3D%22para192%22%20ilmid%3D%22bl4rs%22%20type%3D%22par%22%20language%3D%22en%22%7D)). Unit Conventions are held in October, and the National Convention in spring ([Spiritual Institutions: The Foundation for Oneness](https://bahai-library.com/692)).

I can look further into the 2007 or 1996 letters, or into how the Guardian describes the "silent and prayerful" character of elections.

messages.content: Current UHJ guidance on climate change?

perplexity.text: (error 429)

current.text:
The House of Justice's most direct word on climate change is a letter of 29 November 2017 "to three individuals." The library holds only its catalogue entry, not the full text. That entry describes it as a letter on the science behind human-caused global warming and on how Bahá'ís might take part in activism and awareness-raising while avoiding political divisiveness ([List all documents by Universal House of Justice](https://bahai-library.com/author/Universal_House_of_Justice)). A web summary, which is not scripture and which I couldn't check against the letter, says the following:
- Bahá'ís may contribute actively on the issue.
- They should avoid partisan politics.
- They should not present scientific conclusions as religious belief or obligation.
- They are not required to hold uniform views on climate science or policy.

Treat that as unconfirmed until you read the letter itself.

**Earlier guidance on the environment**
- In the Six-Year Plan period, the House sent National Assemblies the compilation *Conservation of the Earth's Resources*. It was meant to deepen the believers' appreciation of "the Bahá'í concept of nature" and their understanding of "man's relationship to nature and his responsibility to preserve the world's ecological balance" ([Six-Year Plan, 1986-1992](https://bahai-library.com/882)).
- The same letter hoped the friends would assist those striving to make the world "an earthly paradise" ([Six-Year Plan, 1986-1992](https://bahai-library.com/882)).
- The House also set up an Office of the Environment. It handles the Bahá'í International Community's external relations on environmental matters, including relations with the World Wide Fund for Nature and similar organizations ([Six-Year Plan, 1986-1992](https://bahai-library.com/882)).

**The wider frame: social action**
- The House treats environmental and other social concerns as part of social action. Its Riḍván 2010 message says the coming world civilization "must achieve a dynamic coherence between the material and spiritual requirements of life" ([Social Action](https://oceanlibrary.com/social-action_bahaullah/?paraId=para_407&selectionString=social_action_ocean_en-blai.0~social_action_ocean_en-blai.1693)).
- It also says involvement in the life of society "should not be sought prematurely" and grows as the community's capacity grows ([Social Action](https://oceanlibrary.com/social-action_bahaullah/?paraId=para_408&selectionString=social_action_ocean_en-blaj.0~social_action_ocean_en-blaj.705)).

**The boundary of non-partisanship**
- The House has written that working for one political party against another "is a negation of the very spirit of the Faith" ([Daily Lessons Received at 'Akká](http://bahai-library.com/goodall_cooper_daily_lessons)).
- Shoghi Effendi's guidance allowed affiliation with "scientific, humanitarian, industrial, educational and civic affairs" ([Administration and World Order](https://siftersearch.com/library/bahai/pilgrim-notes/mary-maxwell_administration-and-world-order#p162)). That is why climate work can be pursued without taking a party line.

I can look for more of the House's recent statements on climate or on social action if you'd like.

messages.content: Has the House of Justice changed its guidance on membership in political parties over the years? What is current?

perplexity.text:
Yes—but the change has been in **application and clarification**, not in the underlying principle. The Universal House of Justice continues to uphold Bahá’u’lláh’s and Shoghi Effendi’s principle that Bahá’ís should avoid partisan political activity and political-party identification.[1][2]

Historically, the guidance was stated broadly as **non-membership in political parties and political organizations**. Shoghi Effendi described the expected conduct as “non-identification with political parties” and “non-membership in political organizations.”[1]

The House of Justice has nevertheless recognized exceptional circumstances:

- If party membership is legally compulsory, a Bahá’í should, where possible, pay the equivalent dues without formally joining.
- If that is impossible, membership may be accepted reluctantly, but the Bahá’í must not become active—for example, by holding party office.[1]
- Membership should not be accepted merely because it is encouraged, rewarded, or pressured by authorities when the law does not require it.[1]

More recent guidance places greater emphasis on distinguishing **partisan politics** from participation in the life of society. In its 23 December 2008 letter, the House stated that partisan political activity remains prohibited, while constructive discourse and action for social change are encouraged. It also acknowledged that changing social conditions may require further guidance on how to apply the principle.[2]

**Current position:** A Bahá’í should not join or identify with a political party, participate in partisan political activity, campaign for parties or candidates, or hold partisan office. Bahá’ís may engage in nonpartisan civic affairs, social action, public discourse, and government or community service, provided these do not involve partisan political activity. Legally compulsory membership remains an exceptional case governed by the safeguards above.[1][2]

current.text:
No. The House of Justice has not changed the principle: Bahá'ís do not belong to political parties. What it has added over the years is detailed guidance on borderline cases, such as one-party states, voting, and collaboration with opposition movements.

**The principle (Shoghi Effendi, continued by the House)**
- Shoghi Effendi set out "non-acceptance of political posts, non-identification with political parties, non-participation in political controversies, and non-membership in political organizations and ecclesiastical institutions" ([Disinvestment: Is It a Baha'i Issue?](https://bahai-library.com/nirou_divestment_south_africa)) as a standard of Bahá'í conduct ([Crisis and Victory](https://oceanlibrary.com/crisis-and-victory_bahaullah/?paraId=para_363&selectionString=crisis_and_victory_bahai_ocean_en-bld0.0~crisis_and_victory_bahai_ocean_en-bld0.911)).
- In 1968–73 the House of Justice stated the reasoning: "Membership in any political party, therefore, necessarily entails repudiation of some or all of the principles of peace and unity proclaimed by Bahá'u'lláh. As 'Abdu'l-Bahá stated: 'Our party is God's party — we don't belong to any party.'" ([Daily Lessons Received at 'Akká](http://bahai-library.com/goodall_cooper_daily_lessons))
- A letter on Shoghi Effendi's behalf gives the same logic. If each Bahá'í joined a different party, "Where is our unity then?" ([The Light of Divine Guidance (Volume I)](https://oceanlibrary.com/light-of-divine-guidance-volume-i_shoghi-effendi/?paraId=para_933&selectionString=light_of_divine_guidance_volume_1_ocean_en-blqf.0~light_of_divine_guidance_volume_1_ocean_en-blqf.844))
- The House has said Bahá'ís "do not engage in political activities nor belong to political parties." They may do non-political administrative work with governments and hold appointive posts that are not political in character ([Lights of Guidance](https://oceanoflights.org/lights-of-guidance-baha-i-ocean-en/#:~:text=In%20the%20case%20of,%7Bid%3D%22para5529%22%20ilmid%3D%22bl3ik%22%20type%3D%22par%22%20language%3D%22en%22%7D)).

**Clarifications that look like shifts but are not**
- **Voting.** Shoghi Effendi allowed voting only where it does not mean identifying with a party. The friends "may vote, if they can do it, without identifying themselves with one party or another" ([Directives from the Guardian](https://oceanlibrary.com/directives-from-the-guardian_shoghi-effendi/?paraId=para_730&selectionString=directives_from_the_guardian_en-bln3.0~directives_from_the_guardian_en-bln3.702)). The House repeated this in 1998: Bahá'ís may vote for political posts "only when they can do so upon a non-party line, without affiliating themselves with any political party or organization" ([Messages to Canada](https://oceanlibrary.com/messages-to-canada_shoghi-effendi?paraId=fn_19)).
- **One-party states.** The House gave a graded answer:
  - If membership is only encouraged or rewarded, Bahá'ís "should refrain from joining the party, whatever the personal sacrifices may be" ([Lights of Guidance](https://oceanoflights.org/lights-of-guidance-baha-i-ocean-en/#:~:text=2.%20a.%20If%20the,%7Bid%3D%22para5506%22%20ilmid%3D%22bl3hx%22%20type%3D%22par%22%20language%3D%22en%22%7D)).
  - If the law requires every citizen to belong, they may pay the equivalent of the dues without accepting membership ([Lights of Guidance: A Bahá’í Reference File](https://siftersearch.com/library/bahai/compilations/helen-hornby_lights-of-guidance-a-bahai-reference-file#p5188)).
  - If even that is not possible, they "have no choice but to accept membership, without becoming active in the party, such as holding offices" ([Lights of Guidance: A Bahá’í Reference File](https://siftersearch.com/library/bahai/compilations/helen-hornby_lights-of-guidance-a-bahai-reference-file#p5189)).
- **New believers.** The House advised that no extra requirements be laid on them at declaration. They should be told of the Faith's position beforehand, and any remaining political ties should be dealt with by "lovingly and patiently" educating them ([Lights of Guidance](https://oceanoflights.org/lights-of-guidance-baha-i-ocean-en/#:~:text=No%20additional%20requirements%20should,%7Bid%3D%22para5518%22%20ilmid%3D%22bl3i9%22%20type%3D%22par%22%20language%3D%22en%22%7D)).

**Current guidance (2013 onward)**
- On 2 March 2013 the House sent a message on non-involvement in partisan politics to the believers in Iran, copied to all National Spiritual Assemblies ([Bahá'í Library Online](https://bahai-library.com/ris/4328)). A later reply calls non-involvement in politics a principle that "cannot be disregarded by any individual or institution" ([Participation in Politics and Social Activities](https://bahai-library.com/uhj_politics_social_activities)).
- That reply says collaborating with, supporting or approving political parties in opposition to a government "is indeed" a form of involvement in politics. Believers must learn "to strictly abstain, by word and deed, from involvement in partisan politics." They may still take part in civil activities and collaborate with groups whose goals and approaches fit the Faith, without compromising its principles ([Participation in Politics and Social Activities](https://bahai-library.com/uhj_politics_social_activities)).

Shoghi Effendi's own letters also say Bahá'ís can affiliate with "scientific, humanitarian, industrial, educational and civic affairs," but not with political bodies ([Pilgrimage, Volume II (alternate)](https://siftersearch.com/library/bahai/pilgrim-notes/may-and-mary-maxwell_pilgrimage-volume-ii-alternate#p155)). I did not find a more recent House letter that changes the principle on party membership.

messages.content: What does John 14:6 say?

perplexity.text:
John 14:6 (NIV) says:

> “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”[1]

current.text:
John 14:6 reads: "Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me." ([The Bible (KJV), The Gospel of John](https://oceanlibrary.com/kjv-gospel-of-john/?paraId=para_532&selectionString=the-gospel-of-john_en_hg.0~the-gospel-of-john_en_hg.168)) Jesus says it in reply to Thomas, who had just asked, "Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?" ([The Bible (KJV), The Gospel of John](https://oceanlibrary.com/kjv-gospel-of-john/?paraId=para_532&selectionString=the-gospel-of-john_en_hg.0~the-gospel-of-john_en_hg.168))

The Bahá'í Writings read the verse through the idea that the Manifestation is the only channel to knowledge of God. Bahá'u'lláh writes that the door to knowledge of the Ancient Being "hath ever been, and will continue for ever to be, closed in the face of men." ([Bahá’í Sacred Writings](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-sacred-writings/?paraId=para_27&selectionString=baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl3d.0~baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl3d.878)) In mercy God has sent "the Day-Stars of His divine guidance," and has made knowledge of them "identical with the knowledge of His own Self." ([Bahá’í Sacred Writings](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-sacred-writings/?paraId=para_27&selectionString=baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl3d.0~baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl3d.878)) He adds: "Whoso recognizeth them hath recognized God." ([Bahá’í Sacred Writings](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-sacred-writings/?paraId=para_27&selectionString=baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl3d.0~baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl3d.878)) He also calls each of them "the Way of God that connecteth this world with the realms above." ([Bahá’í Sacred Writings](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-sacred-writings/?paraId=para_27&selectionString=baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl3d.0~baha_i_sacred_writings_en-bl3d.878))

'Abdu'l-Bahá explains Jesus' language of "Father" and "Son" in the same way. It is "allegorical and symbolical", like a mirror in which the sun becomes resplendent. A mirror that says "The light is in me" speaks truly, and so "Jesus was truthful when he said, 'The Father is in me.'" ([Divine Philosophy](https://oceanlibrary.com/divine-philosophy_abdul-baha/?paraId=para_595&selectionString=abdu_l_baha_on_divine_philosophy_bahai_ocean_en-blja.0~abdu_l_baha_on_divine_philosophy_bahai_ocean_en-blja.251)) On this reading, "no man cometh unto the Father, but by me" ([The Bible (KJV), The Gospel of John](https://oceanlibrary.com/kjv-gospel-of-john/?paraId=para_532&selectionString=the-gospel-of-john_en_hg.0~the-gospel-of-john_en_hg.168)) describes the Manifestation as the mirror of God. It does not limit access to one historical person.

I can also look for 'Abdu'l-Bahá's or Shoghi Effendi's comments on the verse, if you'd like.

perplexity.text:
**Qur’an 2:255 — Ayat al-Kursi**

اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ

**Translation:**  
Allah—there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.[1]

messages.content: Bhagavad Gita 2:47 — the verse about the right to work but not the fruits.

perplexity.text:
**Bhagavad Gita 2:47**

> कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।  
> मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥ २.४७ ॥

**Transliteration:**

*Karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana;*  
*mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stv akarmaṇi.*

**Translation:**

“You have a right to perform your duty, but not to the fruits of your actions. Do not let the results of action be your motive, and do not become attached to inaction.”[1][2]

The verse teaches disciplined action without attachment to outcomes: focus on performing one’s duty well, while accepting that results depend on causes beyond one’s control. It does **not** mean indifference or passivity; Krishna also warns against using detachment from results as an excuse not to act.[2][10]

current.text:
Bhagavad Gita 2:47 is Krishna's central teaching on *karma-yoga* to Arjuna. You have a right to the action itself, never to its results, so you act without being driven by the reward and without sliding into inaction. The library holds the Gita as [*The Bhagavad-Gita*](https://siftersearch.com/library/view?doc=21038), and the verse falls in the passage that begins "Hear now the deeper teaching of the Yog" ([The Bhagavad-Gita](https://oceanlibrary.com/bhagavad-gita/?paraId=para_36&selectionString=bhagavad-gita_en_3u.0~bhagavad-gita_en_3u.1344)). My search only returned the start of that passage, so I can't quote the verse line itself.

The surrounding lines show how the verse is framed:

- **Disinterested action.** Right after the verse, Krishna says "Scorn them that follow virtue for her gifts!" ([The Bhagavad-Gita](https://oceanlibrary.com/bhagavad-gita/?paraId=para_37&selectionString=bhagavad-gita_en_3v.0~bhagavad-gita_en_3v.651)). Those who act from devotion "seek no gain" and so rise "forth from the bands of body, step by step" ([The Bhagavad-Gita](https://oceanlibrary.com/bhagavad-gita/?paraId=para_37&selectionString=bhagavad-gita_en_3v.0~bhagavad-gita_en_3v.651)). This is the "fruits" teaching applied: the reward-seeking mind stays bound by its deeds.
- **Not a call to idleness.** Chapter 3 says no one escapes action by refusing it. The verse is about the inner motive of an act, not only its outward form.

In the Bahá'í Writings, the nearest passage in the library is 'Abdu'l-Bahá's tablet on self-renunciation. It cites the Gita (chapters 17, 12 and 6) as an example of a teaching found "in all previous dispensations": the devotee surrenders his actions to God and subdues the self ([Tablet to Ismael on Annihilation in God (Lawh-i-Isma'il)](https://bahai-library.com/abdulbaha_lawh_ismael)). That note doesn't cite 2:47 itself.

You may be thinking of Bahá’u’lláh’s **Hidden Words**, Arabic no. 3:

> “Veiled in My immemorial being and in the ancient eternity of My essence, I knew My love for thee; therefore I created thee, have engraved on thee Mine image and revealed to thee My beauty.”

A related passage says:

> “Love Me, that I may love thee. If thou lovest Me not, My love can in no wise reach thee.”

The wording “nothing compares to the love of God” is likely a paraphrase rather than an exact quotation. Another close passage appears in *The Hidden Words*: “There is no peace for thee save by renouncing thyself and turning unto Me… since I desire to be loved alone and above all that is.”[1]

messages.content: Who compiled the first English book of Bahá’í prayers and when?

perplexity.text: The first English book of Bahá’í prayers was compiled by **Anton Haddad** and published in **1897** (some bibliographies date it to **1897 or 1900**) under the title *Tablets, Communes and Holy Utterances*. It is described as the first prayer book and first compilation of Bahá’í writings published in the West.[4]

current.text:
The first English Bahá'í prayer book was probably *Tablets, Communes and Holy Utterances*. It was most likely translated by Anton Haddad and published in Chicago by the Behais Supply and Publishing Board. Sources disagree on the date. Collins gives 1897, and other sources give 1900. The library's chronology describes it as the "First prayer book and first compilation of Bahá'í writings published in West." ([Chronology: Date 1897-00](https://bahai-library.com/chronology/1897-00))

- Most of the selections are from Bahá'u'lláh. Pages 18–21 are from 'Abdu'l-Bahá. ([Chronology: Date 1897-00](https://bahai-library.com/chronology/1897-00))
- The attribution to Haddad is hedged in the chronology: "It was probably translated by Anton Haddad." ([Chronology: Date 1897-00](https://bahai-library.com/chronology/1897-00)) Another listing names Haddad as translator and gives the date as "1897 or 1900." ([List all documents by abdu'l-bahá](https://bahai-library.com/author/abdu'l-bah%C3%A1))
- Walbridge's article on prayer says only that "the American Bahá'ís published a prayer book as early as 1900." ([Prayer and Worship](https://bahai-library.com/walbridge_encyclopedia_prayer_worship)) It names no compiler. ([Prayer and Worship](https://bahai-library.com/walbridge_encyclopedia_prayer_worship))

This book is not the familiar *Bahá'í Prayers*. That is a later compilation by the United States Bahá'í Publishing Trust, with editions in 1954–1982 and 2002. ([Bahá'í Library Online](https://bahai-library.com/ris/6911)) Shoghi Effendi had written about a "projected prayer-book" for the general public, to be a "specially prepared compilation of the prayers of Bahá'u'lláh and 'Abdu'l-Bahá." ([Bahá’í Administration](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-administration_shoghi-effendi/?paraId=para_410&selectionString=baha_i_administration_selected_messages_1922_1932_3521e4ac6904cefdca84fce2627329c7-bld3.0~baha_i_administration_selected_messages_1922_1932_3521e4ac6904cefdca84fce2627329c7-bld3.397))

messages.content: What is the significance of the number 19 in the Bahá’í calendar?

perplexity.text:
The number **19 symbolizes unity** in the Bahá’í tradition. In Arabic abjad numerology, *Váḥid*—meaning “Unity”—has a numerical value of 19; the term also refers to the Báb, together with His 18 first disciples, forming the first “Váḥid.”[8][10]

This symbolism shapes the Bahá’í calendar:

- Each year has **19 months of 19 days**, with four or five intercalary days, called **Ayyám-i-Há**, added to complete the solar year.[4]
- Bahá’ís gather for a **Nineteen Day Feast** at the beginning of each month and observe a **19-day fast** during the final month.[1]
- The calendar also recognizes **19-year cycles**, called *Váḥid*; 19 such cycles form a 361-year period.[7]

Thus, 19 is both a practical organizing principle and a symbolic reference to divine unity and the unity of humanity.

current.text:
The number 19 stands for unity, the oneness of God. The Báb built His calendar on it: 19 months of 19 days each.

**The calendar.** The Badí‘ calendar has nineteen months of nineteen days. Four intercalary days (five in a leap year) are added before the last month, and the year begins at the March equinox, Naw-Rúz ([Sacred Acts, Sacred Space, Sacred Time](https://bahai-library.com/6986)). Another source gives the placement as between the eighteenth and nineteenth months, to bring the calendar into line with the solar year ([bahaullah-st-015_en](https://oceanoflights.org/bahaullah-st-015-en/#:~:text=147.%20.%20The%20Bah%C3%A1%E2%80%99%C3%AD,World%2C%20volume%20XVIII.%20%E2%86%91)). The Báb named the months after attributes of God ([bahaullah-st-015_en](https://oceanoflights.org/bahaullah-st-015-en/#:~:text=147.%20.%20The%20Bah%C3%A1%E2%80%99%C3%AD,World%2C%20volume%20XVIII.%20%E2%86%91)). The first month, Bahá', has a name that also means Glory ([The Kitáb-i-Aqdas](https://oceanlibrary.com/kitab-i-aqdas_bahaullah)). The same calendar gives the nineteen monthly gatherings known as Nineteen Day Feasts ([Sacred Acts, Sacred Space, Sacred Time](https://bahai-library.com/6986)). Shoghi Effendi's secretary describes the Feast as an institution first established by the Báb and later confirmed by Bahá'u'lláh ([The Nineteen Day Feast](https://oceanlibrary.com/nineteen-day-feast_bahaullah/?paraId=para_220&selectionString=the_nineteen_day_feast_bahai_compilation_ocean_en-bl8x.0~the_nineteen_day_feast_bahai_compilation_ocean_en-bl8x.264)).

**Why 19.** The Universal House of Justice explains that the Báb used the numerical value of words to symbolize spiritual concepts. "Váḥid" means "unity" and has the numerical value 19. The number 19 therefore "symbolizes the unity of God", and the Báb used it "as the basis for His Calendar" ([Lights of Guidance](https://oceanoflights.org/lights-of-guidance-baha-i-ocean-en/#:~:text=The%20Bab%20made%20use,%7Bid%3D%22para5239%22%20ilmid%3D%22bl3ak%22%20type%3D%22par%22%20language%3D%22en%22%7D)).

**The first Váḥid.** The eighteen Letters of the Living are called "Ḥurúf-i-Ḥayy", and the value of "Ḥayy" is 18. Together with the Báb Himself they form the first Váḥid ([Lights of Guidance](https://oceanoflights.org/lights-of-guidance-baha-i-ocean-en/#:~:text=The%20Bab%20made%20use,%7Bid%3D%22para5239%22%20ilmid%3D%22bl3ak%22%20type%3D%22par%22%20language%3D%22en%22%7D)). 'Abdu'l-Bahá says the same: the Váḥid of the Bayán "consisteth of the eighteen Letters of the Living and the Báb Himself … Who is the nineteenth" ([Light of the World](https://oceanlibrary.com/light-of-the-world_abdul-baha/?paraId=para_573&selectionString=light_of_the_world_baha_i_ocean_en-blj0.0~light_of_the_world_baha_i_ocean_en-blj0.987)). In a lesson on mystical symbolism He reads the number as 1 + 18. God is expressed in the number 1, and the other eighteen letters are set beside Him as the Letters of the Living. For this reason, He says, the Báb chose 19 "above all for his calendar reform, for the number of His disciples etc." ([Mystical Symbolism Lesson with 'Abdu'l-Bahá](https://siftersearch.com/library/bahai/pilgrim-notes/dr-josephine_mystical-symbolism-lesson-with-abdul-baha#p15)).

**19 × 19.** The Báb also organized His community in groups of nineteen (váḥids) and 361 (kull-i-shay') ([Sacred Acts, Sacred Space, Sacred Time](https://bahai-library.com/6986)). The value of "all things" (kullu shay') is 361, which is 19 × 19. Nader Saiedi explains that all things are therefore manifestations of the Primal Unity ([Gate of the Heart: Understanding the Writings of the Báb](https://siftersearch.com/library/bahai/bahai-books/nader-saiedi_gate-of-the-heart-understanding-the-writings-of-the-bab#p1403)). In his reading, the Bábí solar year takes the same form: 361 days plus the intercalary days ([Gate of the Heart: Understanding the Writings of the Báb](https://siftersearch.com/library/bahai/bahai-books/nader-saiedi_gate-of-the-heart-understanding-the-writings-of-the-bab#p1403)). The Persian Bayán follows the pattern too. It has nine Váḥids, and each of the first eight has nineteen chapters (abwáb) ([A Thematic Analysis and Summary of the Persian Bayán](http://bahai-library.com/terry_analysis_summary_bayan)).

**Other uses.** The House of Justice also points to 19 or 95 mithqals of gold or silver in the laws of marriage and of Ḥuqúqu'lláh ([Lights of Guidance](https://oceanoflights.org/lights-of-guidance-baha-i-ocean-en/#:~:text=The%20Bab%20made%20use,%7Bid%3D%22para5239%22%20ilmid%3D%22bl3ak%22%20type%3D%22par%22%20language%3D%22en%22%7D)).

Mary Maxwell's pilgrim notes record that the Abjad system of letter-values is Muslim in origin. The Báb used it to emphasize the unity of God, of the Prophets and of humanity ([1937, Mary Maxwell — Pilgrim Notes Volume II](https://bahai-library.com/pilgrim_accounts_collection_files/html/1937,%20Mary%20Maxwell,%20Pilgrim%20Notes%20Volume%20II.html)).

I can look further at the names of the nineteen months or at the Nineteen Day Feast, if you'd like.

current.why: This answer has real substance. It covers the calendar's structure, 'Abdu'l-Bahá's own words on the first Váḥid (the Báb plus the 18 Letters of the Living, making 19), a pilgrim note of 'Abdu'l-Bahá reading 19 as 1 + 18, the pattern of 361 = 19 × 19, and the structure of the Bayán. But it rests its central 'why 19' explanation on the Universal House of Justice (Lights of Guidance) before reaching 'Abdu'l-Bahá, which is an authority error. It also leans on Saiedi for symbolic meaning, though it does label him as a scholar.

perplexity.why: Accurate as far as it goes: Váḥid = 19, the first Váḥid, 19 months of 19 days, Ayyám-i-Há, the Feast and the Fast, and the 19-year Váḥid cycle within the 361-year Kull-i-Shay'. But it is thin and close to a truism. Its numbered citations point to no sources, it quotes none of the Writings, and it gives no depth on why the Báb chose 19.

messages.content: When was the Universal House of Justice first elected?

perplexity.text: The Universal House of Justice was first elected on **21 April 1963**, the first day of the Festival of Riḍván, during the First International Bahá’í Convention in Haifa.[1]

current.text:
The Universal House of Justice was first elected on 21 April 1963, the first day of Riḍván, in Haifa. ([Most Great Reconstruction: The Bahá''í Faith in Jim Crow South Carolin…](https://bahai-library.com/venters_bahai_south_carolina)) ([The Institutionalization of Religion: A Sociological Analysis of Relig…](https://bahai-library.com/mahmoudi_institutionalization_religion))

- **Where:** The election took place in the central hall of the home of 'Abdu'l-Bahá and the Guardian in Haifa. ([The Baha'i World: Volume 13 (1954-1963)](https://bahai-library.com/2247))
- **Who voted:** The electors were the members of the 56 National Spiritual Assemblies. Over three hundred of them were present in Haifa. ([The Baha'i World: Volume 13 (1954-1963)](https://bahai-library.com/2247)) Assemblies whose members could not attend took part by absentee ballots sent by mail. ([The Ministry of the Custodians 1957-1963: An Account of the Stewardshi…](https://bahai-library.com/uhj_ministry_custodians&chapter=7))
- **Call for the election:** The Hands of the Cause had called for "a convention in the Holy Land for the election of the Universal House of Justice on the first, second, and third days of Ridván, 1963." ([The Baha'i World: Volume 13 (1954-1963)](https://bahai-library.com/uhj_bahai_world_13))
- **Date and significance:** 21 April 1963 was the centenary of Bahá'u'lláh's arrival in the Riḍván Garden in Baghdad. The election was the crowning achievement of the Ten Year Plan. ([Most Great Reconstruction: The Bahá''í Faith in Jim Crow South Carolin…](https://bahai-library.com/venters_bahai_south_carolina))
- **First members:** Charles Wolcott, ʻAlí Nakhjavani, Borrah Kavelin, Ian Semple, Luṭfu'lláh Ḥakím, David Hofman, Hugh Chance, Amoz Gibson and Hushmand Fatheazam. ([The Covenant](https://oceanlibrary.com/covenant_bahaullah))

The Bahá'í World Congress followed a week later, from 28 April to 2 May 1963. ([Messages from the Universal House of Justice 1963-86](https://bahai-library.com/uhj_messages_1963-86_full&chapter=all))

Universal House of Justice first elected 1963 delegates National Spiritual Assemblies Haifa

current.why: Gives the correct date (21 April 1963) and accurate, useful detail: the house of 'Abdu'l-Bahá, the 56 National Assemblies as electors, absentee ballots, the Hands' call, the Riḍván centenary, all nine first members and the World Congress that followed. Weaknesses: it supports the date with secondary scholarly works (Venters, Mahmoudi) when The Bahá'í World and the Custodians' account were available, and it doesn't say the Congress was held in London.

perplexity.why: Correct and concise, with the date, Riḍván and the First International Convention. But it gives no further substance, and its footnote [1] points to nothing.
